synopsis: The regulator’s 2023 vehicle-interaction paper reported no meaningful year-on-year reduction in reported incidents and an unresolved gap in reliably distinguishing hazardous from spurious conditions; Chapter 4 dates the paper to July, while the glossary says September [f3111, f15539, f3112, f15540, f15537]. Its July 2025 bulletin recorded 30 collisions involving LHD units and personnel transports in underground coal mines over the preceding 12 months, often involving LHDs carrying large loads [f3113, f3114]. Investigations and incident summaries describe a fatal reversing-dozer collision in 2019 and a March 2026 night-time wrong-side driving incident in which two trucks stopped about 15 m apart; secondary accounts of July 2026 incidents still require checking against the regulator’s own text [f3116, f3115, f3117, f3118, f3119]. The regulator is developing a draft Technical Reference Guide on vehicle interaction controls, while its undated brake-formula guidance is a proposal rather than an adopted rule and draws on ISO 3450:1996 and AS 2958.1 [f15538, f5988, f5981]. That brake guidance proposes minimum mean safe net decelerations of 0.60/0.30 m/s² for service/secondary brakes in service and 0.75/0.40 m/s² for type testing, assuming traction and no skidding [f5982, f5983, f5987]. Its worked examples give stopping distances of 34.4 m, 30.82 m and 42.25 m for different truck, speed, loading and grade conditions, so these are scenario-specific examples rather than one universal stopping-distance requirement [f5984, f5985, f5986].
